shots.script: Shot 12 · An AI agent through the MCP server: refused, then paid
Act 3 · The same street, one warm window; then the ask

vo.text: Neighborline is a hotline for neighborhood mutual-aid groups: the volunteers who get cash to neighbors after a storm, a fire or a lost paycheck. Today that runs on English web forms, comment threads and one volunteer's personal Venmo. It's slow, it shuts out people who can't fill in the form, and it's easy to impersonate.

So a neighbor just leaves a voice note, in any language. AI transcribes it, translates it and reads it back. The group's written rules, as code, set the amount. Two organizers approve with passkeys, and PayPal Payouts sends the money to PayPal or Venmo. The AI never decides who gets help, and never touches the money.
Two days after the ice storm, the Eastside is still dark. Mrs. Lan is seventy-one. Her heat is off, and her phone is at twenty-three percent.
She left a voice note, in Vietnamese. Watch the clock.
She heard it read back in Vietnamese and said yes. The group's own rules, not the AI, set the amount: a hundred and fifty dollars. Two organizers sign.

vo.note: "Success." is spoken ~0.7 s after SUCCEEDED is on screen.
vo.text: She claims it. Success. Most payout systems stop at unclaimed; this one follows through.
Someone posing as the organizers, with a Venmo handle one letter off? Approve is disabled on every phone. No money moves.

vo.note: Runs over /trust and into the rail push (Shot 10).
vo.text: Under the hood: the agents that talk to neighbors have no PayPal tools. One separate approval service holds the Payouts credentials, and it pays only on a record signed with the passkeys of two different organizers.
For agent builders: the same guard ships as an MCP server. An AI agent asking to pay is refused without two humans' signatures. With them, it pays.

That night, one window on the Eastside is warm again. Neighborline is open source. Try the hotline yourself; the link is below. Because the morning after a storm, help should sound like your own language.
